finding.claim: wipe() never enforces the OWNER role, so any authenticated user can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled: any User passed to wipe(), including roles={} or {"VIEWER"}; tenant string is also attacker-controlled.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, a destructive tenant-wide delete.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) entry point; POST /tenants/{t}/wipe per comment on line 24.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") called but its boolean result is discarded.
requireRole only returns u.roles().contains(role); doc comment on line 13 says it does not throw, so it cannot block.

finding.guards_checked: requireRole at line 26 is a boolean predicate whose result is ignored, so it is not a guard. No other check in wipe(). checkRole (lines 18-22) would throw correctly but wipe() does not use it. Upstream auth middleware is not in this repo, so unconfirmed whether it blocks non-OWNER callers first.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) is a boolean predicate whose result is discarded at src/Admin.java:26, so it is not effective. checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) would throw but is not called from wipe(). No other guard exists in the repo; the only call sites are src/Admin.java:26-27 and :32.
verdict.reason: wipe() at src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole, whose boolean result (defined at src/Admin.java:14-15) is discarded, so repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 runs for any User that reaches wipe(). The trace matches the code exactly. The only residual uncertainty is upstream auth middleware outside this repo, which could restrict callers, but nothing in the repo enforces OWNER on this path.

finding.claim: export() checks the caller has the OWNER role globally but not that the caller belongs to the target tenant; an OWNER of tenant A could export tenant B.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled tenant string (line 31) and the caller's User, whose global roles set has no tenant field (line 4).
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33, exfiltrating tenant data.

trace.note: User(String name, Set<String> roles) has no tenant identifier, so roles cannot be scoped to a tenant.
export(User u, String tenant) accepts any tenant string from the caller.
checkRole(u, "OWNER") verifies role only; never compares tenant against caller's tenants.
repo.export(tenant) runs for the requested tenant.

finding.guards_checked: checkRole throws correctly, so the role check works. No tenant-membership or ownership check in this file. Exploitability depends on whether the caller can supply an arbitrary tenant, and whether upstream routing restricts tenant to the caller's own tenants; neither is visible here. Lower confidence than ADM-1: confirm before treating as exploitable.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) throws on a missing OWNER role, so the role check works, but nothing in src/Admin.java compares the requested tenant to the caller's tenants. The User record (src/Admin.java:4) has no tenant field, so the file cannot express tenant scoping. The only file in the directory is src/Admin.java, so upstream routing and authorization for /tenants/{t}/export cannot be checked.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (src/Admin.java:31-33: checkRole checks only the global OWNER role, then repo.export(tenant) runs with the caller-supplied tenant), but whether an OWNER of tenant A can reach tenant B depends on upstream routing or ACL logic that is not in the directory, so exploitability cannot be decided from this code.
